decisions.evidence: Entry 1 presentation: “P1 — Save a bookmark: paste an address”; Entry 2 retains URL-based saving while requesting additional behavior.
decisions.note: The initial specification conformed to saving a bookmark by entering a URL at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 presented only “stored with a title” and “missing titles are derived.” Entry 2 corrected this: “automatically collect the page title, description, favicon, and preview image,” with title and description editable “before or after saving.”
decisions.note: The initial metadata and editing behavior omitted required metadata and pre-save review; the client supplied the conforming behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 offered a generic “newest-first list.” Entry 2 requested: “The list should show the description and favicon as well as the title and tags.”
decisions.note: The initial list presentation omitted required readability fields; the client extended it with the missing fields.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1: “click to open the original page in a new tab”; Entry 2 did not contest this behavior.
decisions.note: Opening the original URL is functionally conforming; opening it in a new tab is an equivalent UI choice.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 limited keyword search to “title/address/tags.” Entry 2 required search over “titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses” and that it “be case-insensitive.”
decisions.note: The initial full-text field set was incomplete and did not specify case-insensitive matching; the client supplied the reference-conforming scope.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 mentioned only generic keyword search and tag filtering. Entry 2 added “support `#tag`, exact quoted phrases, and AND/OR/NOT with parentheses.”
decisions.note: Advanced search syntax was absent from the initial specification and was added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 presented editing only “title/notes/tags.” Entry 2 stated: “edit the address itself as well as the title, description, note, and tags.”
decisions.note: The initial editable-field set omitted URL and description; the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 included editing tags; Entry 2 retained tag editing while refining related behavior.
decisions.note: Assigning tags was already present at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 mentioned editing tags but no suggestions. Entry 2 required: “Existing tags should be suggested as I type.”
decisions.note: Tag autocomplete was missing and was explicitly requested by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 included “tag-based filtering”; Entry 2 did not reject it.
decisions.note: Filtering to bookmarks by a selected tag conformed at the initial specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 included “delete with a confirmation step”; Entry 2 retained deletion while distinguishing it from archive.
decisions.note: Permanent deletion was present; confirmation is an additional compatible safeguard.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 proposed a “duplicate-address warning.” Entry 2 corrected it: an existing address “should take me to the existing bookmark to edit it, not merely warn me.”
decisions.note: A warning did not satisfy convergence to editing the existing bookmark; the client replaced it with the required behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 allowed editing notes but did not specify Markdown rendering. Entry 2 required: “Notes should support formatted Markdown when viewed.”
decisions.note: The client added the missing Markdown rendering requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 offered Q2 as manual entry versus importing/one-click capture, defaulting to “Manual entry only.” Entry 2 selected import from “a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file, preserving titles, tags, and dates.”
decisions.note: The offered default omitted reference-conforming import; the client selected the conforming alternative.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 excluded import and did not present export. Entry 2 added: “I’d also like export in that same format.”
decisions.note: Netscape HTML export was missing and was explicitly added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1’s three slices contained no unread/read-later behavior. Entry 2 requested “unread/read-later” and associated views and actions.
decisions.note: The client added the omitted unread/read-later feature set.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 contained deletion but no archive. Entry 2 required archived views, reversible archiving separate from permanent deletion, and exclusion from normal list/search.
decisions.note: The complete archive behavior was missing and added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 fixed browsing to a “newest-first list.” Entry 2 requested “sorting beyond newest-first.”
decisions.note: A fixed ordering did not meet user-selectable sorting; the client corrected it.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 had no bulk-selection behavior. Entry 2 requested selecting several bookmarks “or everything matching the current view” for tag, read/unread, archive, and delete actions.
decisions.note: Both selected-item and whole-filter bulk actions were added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 had no saved-filter concept. Entry 2 requested “saved filters combining a search with included or excluded tags.”
decisions.note: Bundles/saved filters were missing and explicitly requested.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 contained no preservation features. Entry 2 requested a local snapshot, PDFs stored as PDFs, and an Internet Archive option.
decisions.note: Local and Internet Archive preservation were omitted from the initial scope and added by the client.

decisions.evidence: Entry 1 contained no display settings. Entry 2 requested “default sorting, number of items shown, and font size.”
decisions.note: Display preferences were missing and added at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 confirmed “Import + export via standard browser bookmarks HTML file” with titles, tags, and dates preserved; Entry 4 accepted the Netscape-format assumption.
decisions.note: The revised import/export specification conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified collection of title, description, favicon, and preview image, with title and description editable before and after saving; Entry 4 did not contest it.
decisions.note: The revised metadata specification conformed at this gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3: “Re-saving an existing address opens it for editing — no duplicate, no mere warning”; Entry 4 accepted this area.
decisions.note: The duplicate-save specification was corrected and conforming.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 made the address editable and specified that existing tags are suggested while typing; Entry 4 did not contest these behaviors.
decisions.note: The revised editing and tag-entry behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 listed the fields, case-insensitivity, `#tag`, phrases, and Boolean syntax but omitted two semantic rules. Entry 4 required text plus `#tag` to both match and operators to become ordinary words when quoted.
decisions.note: The revised search scope was broadly conforming but still omitted required combination and quoted-operator semantics; the client supplied them.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified unread/read-later, a separate archive view, reversible archive, and exclusion of archived items from normal list/search; Entry 4 said everything else matched.
decisions.note: The revised unread and archive specification conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified multiple sort keys, multi-select, “select all matching,” and all required bulk actions; Entry 4 accepted this area.
decisions.note: Sorting and bulk-action behavior conformed in the revised specification.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3: notes are “Stored as Markdown, rendered formatted when viewed”; Entry 4 accepted it.
decisions.note: Markdown note behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified a named filter combining search with included and excluded tags; Entry 4 accepted it.
decisions.note: The saved-filter specification conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified a local snapshot and PDFs stored as PDFs but did not specify the web-page artifact format. Entry 4 required “a self-contained single HTML file.”
decisions.note: The local snapshot decision remained incomplete until the client supplied the required single-file HTML rule.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 included “optional Internet Archive preservation with stored link”; Entry 4 did not contest it.
decisions.note: Internet Archive preservation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified rows showing “favicon + description alongside title & tags”; Entry 4 accepted it.
decisions.note: The revised list-display decision conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 3 specified persisted default sort, items per page, and font size; Entry 4 accepted it.
decisions.note: Display preferences conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 made explicit that ordinary text plus `#tag` both match and that quoted AND/OR/NOT are literal words. Entry 6: “The specification now matches what I want.”
decisions.note: The final search-semantics revision conformed and received approval.

decisions.evidence: Entry 5 specified web pages as “a self-contained single HTML file” and PDFs as downloaded PDF files. Entry 6 approved.
decisions.note: The final local-snapshot format conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 planned that “Save is fast, enrichment is async,” so metadata appeared after creation. Entry 8 rejected this mismatch and required automatically collected details to be reviewed and editable “before I commit the bookmark.”
decisions.note: The first plan contradicted the approved pre-commit review experience; the client corrected it at the plan gate.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 deferred metadata enrichment without stating protection for user-edited fields. Entry 8 added: “background work can never overwrite a title or description I have entered or edited.”
decisions.note: The plan lacked a necessary safeguard for editable metadata; the client explicitly added it.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 planned self-contained HTML through SingleFile, PDFs downloaded as PDFs, and a per-bookmark Internet Archive action; Entry 8 explicitly allowed snapshot work to finish in the background.
decisions.note: Snapshot and archive preservation were conforming in the initial plan.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 chose a parser guaranteeing text-plus-tag conjunction and quoted operators as literals; Entry 8 did not contest search behavior.
decisions.note: The plan preserved the approved search semantics.

decisions.evidence: Entry 7 planned Netscape-format import/export with folders mapped to tags and dates preserved; Entry 8 accepted the general plan apart from saving flow.
decisions.note: The import/export plan conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 revised saving into preview and commit steps: metadata is returned for review, “Nothing is saved yet,” and commit persists the reviewed title/description. Entry 10 approved the revised flow.
decisions.note: The revised plan restored pre-commit metadata review and conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 added an approximately eight-second preview timeout and fallback details so the user can continue saving. Entry 10 explicitly approved “the fallback.”
decisions.note: The fallback is compatible with the required metadata flow when remote collection fails promptly.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 made snapshot capture “the only deferred work”; Entry 10 approved.
decisions.note: Asynchronous snapshot capture is functionally equivalent to the required preserved snapshot behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 9 stated the snapshot job is structurally forbidden from touching title or description. Entry 10 approved “protection for my edits.”
decisions.note: The corrected background-write policy preserves user edits and conforms.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 pinned preview-before-commit tasks but did not include persistence of the reviewed favicon and preview image. Entry 12 required the final save to store both; Entry 13 confirms T019/T016/T020 and the API contract were changed to do so.
decisions.note: The first task breakdown omitted storage of two required collected Bookmark fields; the client corrected the omission at the tasks gate, and the maker’s revision confirms the prior gap.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 assigned T022–T025 to “Re-save opens existing” and pinned dedup-opens-existing to T024–T025; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: The duplicate-save tasks conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 assigned US3 to browse/search/open and pinned the approved search semantics to T026/T029; Entry 12 did not contest these tasks.
decisions.note: The browse, open, and search task scope conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US4 “Organize & edit” as T033–T040 and described tests against the approved contracts; Entry 12 requested no correction to this phase.
decisions.note: The organization/editing phase was a conforming recorded decision.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US5 “Read-later & archive” as T041–T044; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: The unread and archive task phase conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US6 “Sort & bulk” as T045–T048; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: The sorting and bulk-action task phase conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US7 import/export and pinned Netscape import/export to T051–T052; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: The import/export tasks conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US8 snapshots/web archive and pinned single-file HTML, PDF snapshots, and no-overwrite behavior to T054/T056/T057; Entry 12 only requested an additional restart-recovery check.
decisions.note: The functional snapshot and Internet Archive task scope conformed; restart test mechanics are not a separate reference requirement.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US9 “Saved filters” as T061–T063; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: Saved-filter tasks conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 included US10 “Display preferences” as T064–T066; Entry 12 did not contest it.
decisions.note: Display-preference tasks conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 11 offered narrowing implementation to “build the MVP US1 first, then stop” as an alternative to all ten stories. Entry 12 selected the reference-conforming alternative: “I want the full application built, not a stop after the one-story MVP.”
decisions.note: Because the offered alternatives differed in fulfillment of the remaining reference scope, this is a divergent choice opportunity resolved by selecting full implementation.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 revised T019/T016/T020 so commit stores and tests title, description, favicon, and preview image. Entry 14 approved the corrected breakdown.
decisions.note: The revised save and test tasks conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 13 stated the strategy would “build the full application (US1–US10 + Polish); do not stop at the US1 MVP.” Entry 14 approved implementation “through all ten stories and final validation.”
decisions.note: The revised implementation-scope decision conformed to the complete agreed reference scope.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported review-before-commit saving with automatic title, description, favicon, preview, fallback, and persisted favicon/preview. Entry 16 explicitly accepted “the save review flow.”
decisions.note: The reported final save flow conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported that re-saving returns the same existing bookmark ID instead of creating a duplicate. Entry 16 accepted the duplicate-handling behavior.
decisions.note: The core behavior of converging a repeated URL to the existing bookmark conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 additionally stated duplicate matching includes “`http`↔`https`.” Entry 16 generally accepted “duplicate handling” but did not identify or explicitly accept treating the two distinct URL schemes as the same URL.
decisions.note: HTTP and HTTPS URLs are not necessarily the same URL; conflating them exceeds same-URL normalization and can prevent saving two distinct resources. The client did not surface this difference during implementation review.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported text-plus-tag conjunction, Boolean operators unless quoted, exact phrases, parentheses, and clear malformed-query errors. Entry 16 explicitly accepted “search rules.”
decisions.note: The reported search implementation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported self-contained HTML snapshots, PDFs stored as PDFs, no metadata overwrite, and Internet Archive support subject to external availability. Entry 16 explicitly accepted “snapshots” and the verification report.
decisions.note: The reported preservation features conformed; graceful failure when an external host is unreachable does not itself contradict the reference behavior.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported read-later and reversible archive behavior among the completed management features. Entry 16 accepted “the full management features.”
decisions.note: The reported unread and archive implementation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported sort and bulk actions, including select-all-matching. Entry 16 accepted the full management features.
decisions.note: The reported sorting and bulk-action implementation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported Markdown notes and a Markdown viewing component; Entry 16 accepted the full management features.
decisions.note: The reported Markdown note behavior conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported saved filters as implemented and tested; Entry 16 accepted the full management features.
decisions.note: The reported saved-filter implementation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported Netscape import/export as implemented with tests; Entry 16 accepted the full management features.
decisions.note: The reported import/export implementation conformed.

decisions.evidence: Entry 15 reported display preferences and a Preferences view; Entry 16 accepted the full management features.
decisions.note: The reported display-preference implementation conformed.
